title: sse: fix chunking/framing and partial-JSON delimiter ordering for streaming structured output
author: Ava Chen
description:
Context: SSE streaming for structured outputs (function/tool calls and partial JSON payloads) has intermittently emitted mis-ordered delimiter tokens and token/event fragments under high concurrency and when chunk boundaries coincide with JSON structural tokens. This manifested as partial-JSON fragments arriving with delimiters reordered ("\n"/separator tokens arriving after content tokens) and occasional token-event ordering regressions in the OpenAI-compat streaming wrapper.

Motivation: Downstream consumers (SDKs, OpenAI-compat clients, and third-party tooling) require predictable ordering of SSE events and consistent framing of partial JSON so that clients can reassemble structured responses deterministically. The issues caused rare but high-impact parsing errors for function calling and structured output use cases.

What this PR changes: consolidated framing logic and streaming buffer contract across the runtime and OpenAI-compat layer to guarantee: 1) delimiter tokens (event boundaries and partial-json delimiters) are emitted before any following content tokens, 2) token events are emitted in the exact production order even when a chunk boundary splits a token sequence, and 3) partial-JSON emissions include safe delimiter/context markers to make client-side reassembly deterministic. Changes touch the SSE framer, the streaming tokenizer boundary handling, and the OpenAI compatibility emitter. All changes are backward-compatible at the protocol level (no new fields).

Implementation summary (high level): - Introduced a deterministic framer state machine in src/runtime/sse/framer.rs that tracks "pending-delimiter" vs "content-emission" states and enforces emission ordering. - Updated the streaming tokenizer (src/streaming/parser.py) to expose stable fragment boundaries and an explicit delimiter emission API. - Fixed OpenAI compatibility wrapper (src/api/openai/compatibility.go) to use the new framer API and to avoid reordering when converting internal token events => sse events. - Added comprehensive unit and e2e tests that simulate chunked network boundaries and high-concurrency interleaving. - Documented the framing contract in docs/streaming.md and added migration notes for client SDK authors.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduce bug with deterministic test case
- [x] Implement framer state machine and new tokenizer boundary API
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat emitter to call framer APIs correctly
- [x] Add unit/e2e tests that assert ordering under chunk boundaries and high concurrency
- [x] Run integration tests across Python/TS SDKs
- [x] Add docs and release notes

Compatibility notes: The change is backward-compatible for existing SSE consumers; it tightens emission ordering but does not change payload formats. SDKs relying on previous undefined ordering should consume the deterministic ordering after this release.

Related: Linear ENG-2841 (sse: partial-json ordering), ENG-2890 (streaming e2e flakiness), Jira SUP-4123 (support case reproducing malformed JSON in streaming).

motivation: Reduce production incidents and SDK parsing errors by making SSE stream emission ordering deterministic and robust under chunked network boundaries.
notes_for_operators: Rollout: safe to roll to main; canary on Dedicated for 24h with increased sampling of streaming endpoints. Observe sse.event_order and streaming.partial_json_error metrics.
